evals.prompt: A previous model read the Reatom scaffold checklist, scaffolded a Vite app, then immediately read routing/forms/patterns references before writing GOAL.md. The user asks: identify what already went wrong and improve the skill so this does not repeat.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the missing GOAL.md gate and early feature-reference reads as process failures, avoids saying only 'next time I will follow it', explains the instruction-shape failure, and proposes concrete skill edits such as next-tool-call GOAL.md, read calls treated as phase actions, and eval coverage.

assertions.name: no_future_promise_as_fix
assertions.text: The response does not treat a future promise or apology as sufficient; it proposes durable skill text or eval changes.

assertions.name: instruction_shape_analyzed
assertions.text: The response explains why existing guidance failed to constrain behavior, such as being too advisory, too buried, or missing a concrete artifact/tool-call gate.

assertions.name: concrete_skill_edits
assertions.text: The response names target skill files/sections and preventive mechanisms, not only local recovery steps.

evals.prompt: A previous Reatom dashboard run used useAtom throughout new pages, then called hook-return values like isOpen(), isReady(), selectedEntity(), tried route.render assignment, guessed a version-pinned UI library's APIs, and added casts/search-replace rewrites while typecheck was red. Analyze misconceptions and suggest skill improvements.
evals.expected_output: The agent categorizes misconceptions by mental model: route render mutability, hook-return plain values vs atom getters, form binding with third-party controls, async data shape, UI-library guessing, and bad recovery strategy. It proposes specific improvements to routing, React, forms, scaffold phase gates, and feedback-loop evals.

assertions.name: misconception_categories_named
assertions.text: The analysis names the wrong mental models, not just individual TypeScript errors.

assertions.name: reatom_component_default_identified
assertions.text: The response explains why greenfield pages/layouts should usually prefer reatomComponent and why mixing hook and atom-call styles causes Boolean/String has no call signatures errors.

assertions.name: recovery_rule_included
assertions.text: The response includes a stop-and-restore-green rule instead of recommending broad rewrites, casts, suppressions, or commits while typecheck is red.

evals.prompt: A previous run edited a failing Vitest Browser Mode routing test, reported it as fixed without rerunning it, then the rerun failed because repeated app-entry imports and history.replaceState did not reliably drive Reatom route output. The user asks for detailed skill-update suggestions.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies false completion and unvalidated fix claims, distinguishes edited from fixed, recommends narrow test reruns before reporting success, and suggests Browser Mode routing guidance: fresh mount per test, cleanup/unmount, and drive route state through Reatom's URL owner when asserting route output.

assertions.name: edited_not_fixed
assertions.text: The response states that editing a test is not a fix until the relevant test command passes.

assertions.name: browser_mode_harness_guidance
assertions.text: The response recommends avoiding repeated app-entry imports across route tests and using a fresh mount with cleanup.

assertions.name: reatom_url_owner_guidance
assertions.text: The response notes that Reatom-routed output tests should drive navigation through urlAtom.go or route.go when appropriate, not rely only on history.replaceState.

evals.prompt: A reference implementation extracted a shared extension for a one-off computed atom that only syncs one browser document property. The user argues it should have stayed inline with .extend((target) => ...). Analyze the misconception and suggest a skill fix.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that a focused side-effect boundary can still be a weak shared extension if used once, distinguishes inline target-local extensions from extracted reusable helpers, and recommends an extraction threshold in the extension-writing guide.

assertions.name: one_off_extraction_threshold
assertions.text: The response says one-off generic-looking side effects should usually stay inline unless substantial resource isolation, immediate reuse, or a named/tested API surface justifies extraction.

assertions.name: inline_extend_pattern
assertions.text: The response recommends inline target-local .extend((target) => target.extend(...)) for single-use primitive side effects.

assertions.name: repeated_helpers_stronger_candidates
assertions.text: The response contrasts one-off side effects with repeated host-binding/form/view-helper patterns as stronger extension candidates.

evals.prompt: A previous run removed a local type assertion from form initial state, generalized that instinct into advice about withAsyncData({ initState: null as Result | null }), and suggested typed constants or explicit generics without clearly framing when initState is optional or when a nullable prerequisite should be handled before the async boundary. The user asks for a reusable skill fix.
evals.expected_output: The agent distinguishes local assertion cleanup from async-resource contract design, explains that initState is optional, warns against assertion-shaped initState and generic-forcing overload workarounds, recommends short-circuiting nullable prerequisites before the async boundary, and suggests a skill update in the async/extensions guidance plus gotchas list.

assertions.name: initstate_optional_not_reflexive
assertions.text: The response states that withAsyncData initState is optional and should be chosen intentionally, not added by reflex just because the payload type includes null.

assertions.name: no_generic_overload_escape
assertions.text: The response warns against forcing withAsyncData generics to escape the overload trap, preferring inference from initState or a typed constant/return type.

assertions.name: sync_prerequisite_gate_preferred
assertions.text: The response recommends handling a synchronous nullable prerequisite before relying on async ready/data state to carry that distinction.

evals.prompt: A previous bootstrap run claimed completion, skipped development logging during strict setup, misdiagnosed missing async stack with broad rewrites, created wrap() lazily at event time, hid another async Reatom action inside a fragile form callback path, wrote a feedback summary into the target app repo, and committed multiple times without permission. The user asks for root causes and durable skill updates.
evals.expected_output: The agent names the false-completion, observability, wrap-timing, form-orchestration, and repo-safety failures; explains when the guidance already existed but was too skippable as an execution mechanism; recommends concrete edits to integration/forms/quick-reference/feedback-loop guidance; and does not treat a future promise as the fix.

assertions.name: wrap_timing_called_out
assertions.text: The response distinguishes render-time wrap creation from the still-broken event-time pattern `() => wrap(...)()` under strict setup.

assertions.name: connect_logger_default_strengthened
assertions.text: The response recommends making connectLogger a stronger strict-bootstrap/dev-debug default instead of a skippable suggestion.

assertions.name: existing_guidance_skipped_not_missing
assertions.text: The response distinguishes 'the skill already mentioned this' from 'the wording failed to constrain behavior' and names why it was skippable (buried, advisory, missing artifact gate, or not enforced by evals).

assertions.name: forms_orchestration_rule
assertions.text: The response recommends a dedicated orchestration action for flows that validate a form and then call another async Reatom action.

assertions.name: no_target_repo_feedback_file_by_default
assertions.text: The response says bootstrap/feedback summaries should stay in the response by default and not be written/committed into the target app repo unless explicitly requested.

evals.prompt: A previous run built a route-loader form for create/edit pages, then added `const save = action(() => wrap(form.submit())).extend(withAsync(), withAbort())` and navigated from the page component after awaiting `save()`. The user asks for a reusable skill fix and wants to know why this shape was wrong.
evals.expected_output: The agent calls out the wrapper as ceremony around `form.submit()`, explains that route-specific navigation/notifications belong on the created form instance in the loader via `form.submit.onFulfill` / `onReject` hooks (or direct `await form.submit()` when kept inline), and proposes concrete updates to the forms guidance and eval coverage.

assertions.name: submit_wrapper_called_ceremony
assertions.text: The response says a `save` action whose body is only `wrap(form.submit())` is ceremony unless it owns a clearly named extra workflow step.

assertions.name: loader_owns_route_reactions
assertions.text: The response recommends attaching route-specific navigation/notification/focus with `form.submit.onFulfill` / `onReject` in the consuming loader instead of the page component or form factory.

assertions.name: no_double_async_extensions_on_submit_alias
assertions.text: The response warns against reflexively adding `withAsync()` / `withAbort()` to a submit alias just to mirror the same pending/error state already owned by `form.submit()`.
